title: Leaders From Both Parties Back a New Bike and Walking Bridge Over the Ohio River
summary:
The Market Street Bridge stretches almost 1,800 feet across the Ohio River, linking downtown Steubenville, Ohio, with Weirton, West Virginia. But the old steel bridge closed in late 2023 after cables anchoring it failed. Officials say it is beyond repair.

"You got severe rusting under here," said Michael Paprocki, a regional transportation planner, pointing to holes in the beams.

Local leaders want a replacement for two reasons. First, the closed bridge was the only safe way for people on foot or bikes to cross, and the only bridge leading cars straight into downtown. Maura Barnes, who helps run a grocery store in downtown Steubenville, said nearby businesses saw fewer visitors after it closed.

Second, the river is a big gap in the Great American Rail-Trail, a plan to turn old railroad routes into bike and walking paths stretching about 3,700 miles across the country. More than half of the trail already exists, said Eric Oberg of the Rails to Trails Conservancy, the nonprofit behind it.

The plan has support from both political parties. Steubenville's Republican mayor, Ralph Petrella, called it "huge" for his city. Weirton's Democratic mayor, Dean Harris, worked at a steel mill for 48 years before it closed in 2024. He said trails can help attract new businesses and jobs for future generations.

A new bridge with a separate bike and walking path is planned a few blocks away. Congress has set aside $87 million so far, but that is only part of the cost. Local leaders are asking lawmakers for more money at a time when the Trump administration has opposed federal spending on bike projects.

Oberg is hopeful. "It's gonna happen," he said. "The question is the timeline."
why_it_matters: The project shows how a single bridge can affect jobs, shops and travel for whole communities. It is also an example of leaders from both parties working together on a shared goal.

background_read: Rail-trails are walking and biking paths built on old railroad routes that trains no longer use.
The Great American Rail-Trail is a plan to link many of these paths into one route across the United States, but large rivers create gaps that need bridges.
The Ohio River forms part of the border between Ohio and West Virginia, so bridges are vital for people who live, work and shop on both sides.
Big bridge projects often depend on money from Congress and the states, so local leaders must persuade lawmakers to fund them.
